clue.text: Queen taking a gamble clasping snake? On the contrary

indicators.note: flips the stated relationship, so instead of the gamble holding the snake, the snake comes first and the gamble follows it

parts.note: a boa is a large constricting snake
to dice is to gamble, playing with dice
taken as written

explanation.surface: A monarch takes a punt while holding a serpent, or perhaps the serpent holds her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' reverses the picture of a gamble clasping a snake: the snake BOA leads, followed by DICE and A.
explanation.definitionFit: The warrior ruler of the Iceni, also called Boudicca, led a revolt against Roman Britain.

clue.text: Rolling round, cry over books

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece sits over (above) the next

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O
to pule is to whimper or cry feebly
NT, the New Testament, is a set of books

explanation.surface: Someone tumbling about, wailing on top of a pile of books.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Rolling in it' means wealthy, so rolling is slang for rich and lavish.

clue.text: Hedonists not usually disposed to cheat

indicators.note: reads as 'unusually', so the letters are arranged in an unusual way

explanation.surface: Pleasure-seekers are rarely inclined towards deceit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not usually' looks like a qualifier of 'disposed' but it is the anagram signal; the definition is 'disposed to cheat'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone inclined to deceive is untruthful and crooked.

clue.text: Churchman copper brought before judge

indicators.note: the first piece is placed ahead of the second

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
to rate is to assess or judge

explanation.surface: A clergyman's police officer is hauled up before a magistrate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' suggests a policeman, but it is the metal's symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: An assistant parish priest in the Church of England is a clergyman.

clue.text: Left out, manipulate actors cast in Much Ado about Nothing

indicators.note: the letter for left is put out of the mixed letters
the letters are cast, thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A director is told to handle the players in a Shakespeare comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left out' removes L from MANIPULATE ACTORS; 'cast' then rearranges the remaining fifteen letters. The Shakespeare title is the definition, read as a fuss over nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A great fuss over a trivial matter is exactly what the idiom describes.

clue.text: Maroon thread

definitions.meaning: to maroon is to leave someone ..., as on a beach
a single fibre or filament of yarn or hair

explanation.definitionFit: To leave someone stuck ashore, and a single filament, are both senses of the same word.

clue.text: Scatter liquid and soak flowers, missing one on the way up

indicators.note: in a down clue this reads the pieces upwards, so backwards

parts.note: to ret is to soak flax or hemp to soften it

indicators.note: the flower word goes without the letter for one

parts.note: tulips are flowers
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A gardener sprays water and drenches the blooms, one going short, as they climb.
explanation.walkthrough: RET + TULPS (TULIPS 'missing' I) gives RETTULPS; 'on the way up' turns it over in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To spit or spray drops about while speaking is to send out liquid in bursts.

clue.text: After almost a month, bed produces fruit

indicators.note: the bed comes after the shortened month
the month is cut short of its final letter

parts.note: April is a month
a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: Once most of a spring month has passed, the garden plot yields fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bed' suggests a flower bed, but it is a cot.
explanation.definitionFit: An orange-yellow stone fruit related to the peach and plum.

clue.text: West Indian friar

definitions.meaning: a native of the Caribbean island republic sharing Hispaniola with Haiti
a member of the order of preachers founded by St Dominic

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a person from a Caribbean republic and a Black Friar of St Dominic's order.

clue.text: It's simpler without second office on ship

definitions.note: names the shipboard post rather than the person holding it

indicators.note: in the old sense of outside, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: purer means simpler or less mixed

explanation.surface: Something plainer, minus a deputy, is the ship's office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside: PURER wraps around S.
explanation.definitionFit: The ship's officer who keeps accounts, a post or office aboard; the clue's wording names the role by its post.

clue.text: Wire going round old border permitted

indicators.note: turning round means the whole run of letters is read backwards

parts.note: marge is an archaic or poetic word for a margin or edge
let means allowed or permitted

explanation.surface: Barbed wire is strung around an ancient boundary that was allowed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' reverses MARGELET as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: A wire was an old word for a cabled message sent by telegraph.

clue.text: Note by stout journalist

indicators.note: one piece stands right beside the next

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
porter is a dark beer like stout

explanation.surface: A memo beside a portly newspaperman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stout' suggests portly, but it is a beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper writer who gathers and files news stories.

clue.text: One with huge bill wrecking account — hundred short?

indicators.note: the word is wrecked, its letters scrambled
the letters fall short of the letter for a hundred

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Someone facing an enormous invoice ruins their bank balance, a hundred pounds down.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove one C from ACCOUNT ('hundred short') and rearrange the six letters left ('wrecking').
explanation.definitionFit: A tropical American bird famous for its enormous brightly coloured beak.

clue.text: Soak gets over the top

definitions.meaning: to leave to soak in liquid, as tea leaves
excessive, as a price that is far too high

explanation.definitionFit: To immerse in liquid, and an excessive charge, are both senses of the word.

clue.text: One begging to take the place of one inside

indicators.note: the letter for one is placed inside the other piece

parts.note: to supplant is to replace or take the place of
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A petitioner wants to oust the person within.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'One' is in the definition; the second 'one' gives I.
explanation.definitionFit: A humble petitioner who asks earnestly for something.

clue.text: Cat and mice in novel production fit for the screen

indicators.note: a new, novel production rearranges these letters

explanation.surface: A book about a cat and some mice is turned into a film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' suggests a book, but here it says the letters are made new.
explanation.definitionFit: Suitable for, or in the style of, motion pictures.

clue.text: Mullein that produced almonds

definitions.meaning: a tall yellow-flowered plant, Verbascum, known by this folk name
in Numbers 17, the staff of Moses's brother budded and bore almonds

explanation.definitionFit: The biblical staff that blossomed also lends its name to the tall flowering mullein.

clue.text: Witch-hunter's cry — match is rigged

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', a link joining definition to wordplay

indicators.note: a fixed or rigged event has its parts rearranged

explanation.surface: The persecutor's protest: the game was fixed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is rigged' signals the anagram of CRY and MATCH.
explanation.definitionFit: The US senator who led the 1950s anti-communist purges became a byword for political persecution.

clue.text: Slip in London Lane

definitions.meaning: an undergarment worn under a skirt or dress
the word goes in front of 'Lane' to name a famous East London street market

explanation.definitionFit: An underskirt shares its name with the street of the London Sunday market.

clue.text: Monkey's home submerged beneath river

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', a link joining definition to wordplay

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece lies below the first

parts.note: the Tamar is the river dividing Devon and Cornwall
in means at home

explanation.surface: An ape's house lies underwater below the river.
explanation.walkthrough: The TAMAR is the river on the border of Devon and Cornwall in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A small South American primate with silky fur.

clue.text: African port housing grand musical instrument

indicators.note: one piece holds the other inside

parts.note: Oran is a port in Algeria
G is an abbreviation for grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: A North African harbour holding a grand piano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grand' suggests a piano, but it gives G.
explanation.definitionFit: A keyboard instrument sounding through pipes, found in churches.

clue.text: A scholar taken to court over play

parts.note: taken as written
an MA, Master of Arts, is a scholar

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is turned over, read upwards

parts.note: sued means taken to court

explanation.surface: An academic is hauled before the judge about a drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses SUED.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Shaffer's stage drama about Mozart and Salieri.

clue.text: It's essential to bust up organisation in a state of shock

indicators.note: It's essential to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Breaking up the firm leaves everyone dazed.
explanation.definitionFit: A dazed condition with dulled senses, as after a blow.

clue.text: Plate creature rejected

indicators.note: turned back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: an animal is a creature

explanation.surface: A dish is sent back by a beast.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin layer or flat scale of material, as in rock or bone.

clue.text: Foreign pupil hanging around entrance to school

indicators.note: the pupil surrounds the inserted letter

parts.note: an Etonian is a pupil at Eton College

indicators.note: the first letter of the word, its way in

explanation.surface: An overseas student loiters near the school gates.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton is a famous English private school.
explanation.definitionFit: Belonging to a Baltic country, hence from abroad.

clue.text: It's coming back to be eaten by a reptile -a little puzzling

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other, as if swallowed

parts.note: croc is short for crocodile

indicators.note: the word comes back, read in reverse

parts.note: taken as written, its letters then turned

explanation.surface: A creature returns only to be swallowed by a crocodile, which is rather baffling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming back' turns ITS into STI, which goes inside A CROC.
explanation.definitionFit: A word puzzle in which initial letters of lines spell out a hidden word.

clue.text: Piglet, Pooh, Owl, Roo, Kanga, Eeyore, Rabbit all leading characters there?

indicators.note: the leading letters, the first characters of each named friend

explanation.surface: A roll-call of the Hundred Acre Wood's animals, all heads present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piglet' looks like one of the list but is the definition; the list starts at Pooh.
explanation.definitionFit: A young pig fattened for food.

clue.text: Fly back, and take flight without female, in confused state

indicators.note: the word is read back to front

parts.note: a gnat is a small fly

indicators.note: the letter for female is left out of the word

parts.note: to fly is to take flight

explanation.surface: An insect turns back and flees, minus a lady, in a muddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns GNAT into TANG; FLY less F gives LY.
explanation.definitionFit: Knotted and matted, like twisted hair.

clue.text: Show round one's garden

indicators.note: the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: to parade is to show off
I is one, and 's adds S

explanation.surface: Showing a visitor around one's garden.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition refers to the Garden of Eden.
explanation.definitionFit: Eden was the garden of perfect bliss.
